content: Jaro-Winkler favors prefix similarity, good for short strings/names but risks merging distinct short tags with shared prefixes (#thought vs #thoughtful). Levenshtein/edit distance handles typo transpositions better for short strings. Best practice: blocking (group by first chars) then n-gram/cosine prefilter then edit distance on candidates. Thresholds are steep for short strings -- literature reports near-zero false positives only at 0.96-0.99 similarity; below that, false positive (over-merge) rate rises fast because short strings have few characters so each edit changes similarity a lot.
